query_text: What medicine should I take when I get a cold?

content.text:
For a typical **common cold**, there’s no medicine that “cures” it—most colds get better on their own in about **7–10 days**—but OTC medicines can reduce symptoms. Antibiotics usually **don’t help** because colds are caused by viruses. ([mayoclinic.org](https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/common-cold/diagnosis-treatment/drc-20351611?sf237848573=1&utm_source=openai))

**Choose medicine based on your symptoms:**

- **Fever, headache, sore throat, body aches:**  
  **Acetaminophen** or **ibuprofen** can help. Avoid doubling up—many “multi-symptom” cold products already contain acetaminophen.

- **Stuffy nose / congestion:**  
  A **saline nasal spray** is safest. A decongestant may help, but ask a pharmacist/clinician first if you have **high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma, prostate/urination problems**, are pregnant, or take stimulant/MAOI-type medications.

- **Cough:**  
  **Honey** can help cough in adults and children **at least 1 year old**; don’t give honey to babies under 1. Some people use cough medicines like **dextromethorphan** for dry cough or **guaifenesin** for mucus, but benefits vary. ([cdc.gov](https://www.cdc.gov/acute-bronchitis/about/index.html?utm_source=openai))

- **Runny nose / sneezing:**  
  An antihistamine may help, but some can cause drowsiness.

Also: **rest, drink fluids, use a humidifier/steam, and consider testing for COVID or flu** if symptoms fit or you’re high-risk; antivirals may be available for flu/COVID if started early. ([cdc.gov](https://www.cdc.gov/common-cold/treatment/index.html?utm_source=openai))

**Get medical care urgently** if you have trouble breathing, chest pain, blue lips, confusion, dehydration, fever that’s high or lasts more than ~3 days, symptoms worsening after improving, or if you’re very young/older, pregnant, immunocompromised, or have significant chronic illness.

If you tell me your **age**, main symptoms, any medical conditions, and medicines you take, I can help you pick the safest OTC option.
